b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean: # A uniform point of the extended space from the sub-line law
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean: 
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean: The first scalar estimate in the combining argument samples an extended line
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean: from the sub-line witness and then a uniform affine parameter on that line.
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean: This module records that the resulting extended point is uniform and hence
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean: that its two source coordinate blocks are independent uniform points.

b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean: ## References
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean: 
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean: These statements support `lem:claim-17-1` in
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean: `blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex`.  The paper uses this sampling
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean: fact at

b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean: -/

b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean: /-- Reading a point at a uniform affine parameter on the canonical line of a

b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean: scalar coordinates. -/
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean: /-- The two source blocks of a uniform extended point are independent and
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean: uniform after the canonical scalar identification. -/

b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: /-!
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: # Z-point deficits of the evaluated pair-line measurement
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: 
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: This module bounds the deficit of the overlap between the evaluated paired-line
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: measurement and the expanded Z-point measurement. The proof inserts the completed
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: joint point measurement, replaces it by the X-then-Z ordered product, and sums
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: the X effects. It uses evaluated consistency and the distance from the joint
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: point measurement to that ordered product. The bound holds first over any
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: probability law on pairs of line-point pairs and then over a product of restricted
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: line-point laws, whose point marginal is the uniform pair.
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: 
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: The estimates hold for arbitrary opposite placements, with first-player
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: specializations; register commutation requires no symmetry of the state.
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: The completed-outcome and real-overlap lemmas are also available for other
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: calculations. The concrete X-deficit argument is separate, in
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: `MIPStarRE.QPBT.Combining.Lines.ConcreteXDeficit`.
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: 
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: ## References
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: 
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: The Z deficit supports blueprint `lem:claim-17-3-re-direct`, alongside the
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: source `lem:claim-17-3`, paper
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1204-1239`; the
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: consistency input is `lem:qld-xz-lines` and the ordered products are those of

b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: /-! ## Completed point pairs -/
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: /-- A sum over completed outcome pairs of a function vanishing on both `none`
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: classes is the sum over the uncompleted pairs. -/
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: /-- The completed joint measurement has the joint effect on a pair of
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: evaluations. -/
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: /-- The completed joint measurement vanishes on outcomes outside the image of
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: the completion. -/
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: /-- The completion of a projective joint measurement is projective. -/
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: /-- A placed projection is a projection. -/
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: /-- Every effect of the completed expanded point measurement is a projection,
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: the `none` effect being zero. -/
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: /-- The completed joint point measurement and a completed point product differ
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: only on outcome pairs with two evaluations, so their placed state-dependent
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: squared distance is the one of the joint point measurement and the point
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: product.  Blueprint `ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2651-2698`. -/
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: /-- The completed `Z`-then-`X` point product vanishes on both `none` classes
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: and restricts to the ordered product on evaluated pairs. -/
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: /-! ## The abstract one-point deficit -/
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: /-- Let `A` be a complete measurement, `Q` a projective measurement, `R` a
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: family of projections and `W` a family of operators, all indexed by the same
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: outcomes, with `Q`, `R` and `W` commuting with the effects of `A` and with
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: `W R = W`.  If `A` and `Q` are consistent with defect at most `η` and `Q` is
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: within squared distance `ζ` of `Wᴴ`, then the deficit of the overlap of `A`
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: with `R` is at most `2 √η + 2 √ζ`.  The proof inserts `Q` before `R`, replaces
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: `Q R` by `W R = W`, and compares `W` with `Q`; each of the three steps is a
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: Cauchy--Schwarz estimate weighted by `A`.  This is the common estimate behind
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: the deficits in the proofs of `lem:claim-17-2` and `lem:claim-17-3`, paper
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1168-1239`. -/
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: /-! ## The two placed deficits -/
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: /-- A pair of line-point pairs of the source space: the sample type of the
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: consistency display of `lem:qld-xz-lines`. -/
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: /-- The `Z`-point deficit of the evaluated pair-line measurement over a
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: probability law on pairs of line-point pairs, from the consistency of the
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: evaluated pair-line measurement with the completed joint point measurement
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: and the closeness of the latter to the `Z`-then-`X` product.  This is the
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: deficit bounded in the proof of `lem:claim-17-3`, paper
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1204-1239`. -/
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: /-- The original first-player specialization of the opposite-placement estimate. -/
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: /-! ## The two deficits over a product of restricted line-point laws -/
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: /-- Every restricted line-point law has total mass one. -/
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: /-- The point marginal of a restricted line-point law is uniform. -/
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: /-- The pair of points of a product of two restricted line-point laws is a
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: uniform pair. -/
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: /-- A state-dependent distance between two families depending on the pair of
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: points only, averaged over a product of two restricted line-point laws, is the
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: distance averaged over a uniform pair of points. -/
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: /-- The `Z`-point deficit over a product of two restricted line-point laws,
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: with the inflation `4 m ^ 2` of the line consistency error and the inflation
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: `4` of the point consistency error. -/
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: /-- The original first-player specialization of the opposite-placement estimate. -/
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement.lean: /-- An expanded line effect is consistent with itself followed by the expanded
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement.lean: point effect selected by its value at the sampled point. This is item 2 of
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement.lean: `lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper

b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean: # Bipartite estimates and transport for the expanded line measurements
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean: 
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean: This module collects the generic distance estimates used by items 2 and 3 of
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean: the expanded-line consistency lemma, and the identities that transport the
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean: placed families of the six-register expanded state to the two opposite-
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean: placement bipartitions. The generic estimates are: the distance between two
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean: oppositely placed complete measurements is at most twice the complement of
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean: their diagonal overlap (`fact:agreement`), and a projective family compared
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean: with itself followed by an effect selected through a coarse-graining is at
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean: most as far as the coarse-grained families are from each other
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean: (`fact:add-a-proj2` for a projective refinement). The transport identities
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean: are formalization-only auxiliaries: they carry a relation between placed
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean: operators on the six-register expanded state to the product shape in which the
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean: generic estimates are stated, a step the source leaves implicit.

b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean: # Evaluation of line polynomials at a sampled point
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean: 
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean: This module records the elementary calculus of the partial evaluation
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean: `evalOpt` of a coefficient-list line polynomial at a point: the evaluation of
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean: a sum is the sum of the evaluations whenever both summands evaluate, a summand
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean: of an evaluating sum evaluates whenever the other summand does, the value is
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean: unique, and nothing evaluates at a point off the line. These facts underlie
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean: the manipulation of the evaluation classes in items 2 and 3 of the
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean: expanded-line consistency lemma.
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean: 
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean: Every declaration below is a formalization-only auxiliary: the source uses
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean: these facts about evaluation without stating them.
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean: 
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean: ## References
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean: 
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean: The evaluation classes `[eval_u(·) = a]` are `def:ideg-deg-polynomials`, paper
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean: `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:51-58`. They are
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean: manipulated in `eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons` and `eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons2`,
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean: paper `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:534-545`.
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean: -/
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean: /-- Coefficient-list evaluation is additive in the coefficient list. This
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean: is the additivity behind the convolution of `def:expanded-line-measurement`. -/
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean: /-- A line polynomial has at most one value at a point of the line: if it
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean: evaluates both to `a` and to `b`, then `a = b`. -/
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean: /-- The sum of two evaluating line polynomials evaluates to the sum of
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean: their values. This is why the convolution outcome `f = f' + f''` evaluates
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean: whenever both convolution factors do. -/
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean: /-- If a sum and its second summand evaluate, the first summand evaluates to
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean: the difference of their values. This is the converse direction used to identify
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean: the convolution fibers of an evaluation class. -/
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean: /-- The partial evaluation returns `some a` exactly when the polynomial
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean: evaluates to `a`. This is the characterization that makes `evalOpt` the total
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean: form of the evaluation classes of `def:ideg-deg-polynomials`. -/
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean: /-- The partial evaluation returns `none` exactly when no value is
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean: determined. This is the outcome that completes the evaluation classes to a
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean: measurement, written `[eval_u(·) = ⊥]` in `def:ideg-deg-polynomials`. -/
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean: /-- The partial evaluation of a sum of two evaluating line polynomials is
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean: the sum of their values. -/
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean: /-- If a sum and its second summand evaluate, so does the first summand,
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean: with the difference of the two values. -/
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean: /-- A point at which some line polynomial evaluates lies on the line. -/
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean: /-- Off the line, no line polynomial evaluates, so every outcome falls in
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean: the `none` class. -/

b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Expanded.lean: line measurement with the Pauli-register line projectors, and records that the

b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Expanded.lean: measurement is the addition postprocessing, and the evaluation-class and
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Expanded.lean: point-effect families used by the consistency estimates.

b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: # Pauli-register line projectors
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: 
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: This module constructs the projective measurement `tau^{W,line}` of one
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: generalized-Pauli register whose outcome is the restriction to a canonical
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: line of the low-degree encoding of the measured basis label. It records that
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: the outcome projectors are orthogonal projections summing to the identity,
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: that they are symmetric matrices (so that they act identically on either half
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: of an EPR pair), and that on an axis-parallel line they vanish outside the
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: embedded degree-`d` subspace.
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: 
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: ## References
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: 
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: The projectors are `tau^{W,line}_{f''}` of `def:expanded-line-measurement`,
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: with paper source
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:552-556`. Their
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: perfect self-consistency on an EPR pair is the ancillary input to item 1 of
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: `lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:527-532`.
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: -/
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: /-- The Pauli-register projector onto labels whose low-degree encoding
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: restricts to `f` on `line`. This is `tau^{W,line}_f` in the proof of
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: `lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:552-556`, blueprint
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: `def:expanded-line-measurement`. -/
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: /-- Pauli line projectors are positive semidefinite. This is the positivity of
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: the ancillary measurement in `def:expanded-line-measurement`, paper
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:552-556`. -/
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: /-- The line coarse-graining of the generalized Pauli projectors is a
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: symmetric matrix. Symmetry is what makes the projector act identically on
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: either half of an EPR pair, and hence is the hypothesis behind the perfect
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: ancilla consistency used in `enu:qld-comm-line-self-cons`, paper
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:527-532`. -/
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: /-- Pauli line projectors belonging to distinct line polynomials are
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: orthogonal, while each projector is idempotent. This is the ancillary product
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: calculation in `def:expanded-line-measurement` and item 1 of
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: `lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:552-558`. -/
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: /-- The line fibers partition the complete family of Pauli eigenspace
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: projectors. This is the completeness of the ancillary measurement in
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: `def:expanded-line-measurement`, paper
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:552-556`. -/
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: /-- The projective line measurement on one Pauli register obtained by
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: measuring the generalized Pauli basis and restricting the low-degree encoding
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: of the outcome to `line`. This is the ancillary measurement of
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: `def:expanded-line-measurement`, paper
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:552-556`. -/
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: /-- The effects of the Pauli line measurement are the line projectors. -/
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: /-- On an axis-parallel line, Pauli line projectors vanish outside the
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: embedded degree-`d` subspace, because every restricted low-degree encoding has
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: degree at most `d` there. This is the ancillary half of the last assertion of
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: `def:expanded-line-measurement`, paper
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:552-556`. -/
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: /-! ## Interaction with the point projectors -/
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: /-- On a point of the line, Pauli line projectors of non-evaluating
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: polynomials vanish: every restricted low-degree encoding evaluates there.
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: Formalization-only auxiliary for items 2 and 3 of `lem:qld-comm-line-cons`,
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:534-545`. -/
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: /-- A Pauli line projector followed by a Pauli point projector at a point of
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: the line is the line projector when the line polynomial evaluates to the
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: point value, and zero otherwise. This is the exact consistency
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: `tau^{W,line}_{f''}` versus `tau^{W,u}_{f''(u)}` in items 2 and 3 of
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: `lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:534-545`. -/
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: /-- Pauli line and point projectors commute. -/
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: /-- Acting with a Pauli line projector on one half of the EPR state and a
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: Pauli point projector on the other half equals acting with their product on
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: the first half. Formalization-only support for the exact ancillary
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: consistency in items 2 and 3 of `lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:534-545`. -/
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: /-- On an EPR pair, a point projector on the first factor and a line
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: projector on the second act as the product of the two projectors on the first
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: factor alone. This is the transport with the two factors interchanged, and it
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: uses the symmetry of the line projector rather than that of the point
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: projector. Formalization-only auxiliary for the ancillary consistency of
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: `def:expanded-line-measurement`, paper
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:527-532`. -/
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: /-- The EPR quadratic form of a line projector on one half and a point
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: projector on the other half is the EPR quadratic form of the line projector
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: alone when the line polynomial evaluates to the point value, and zero
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: otherwise. This is the exact ancillary consistency in items 2 and 3 of
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: `lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:534-545`. -/
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: /-- The EPR overlap of a point projector on the first factor with a line
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: projector on the second vanishes unless the line polynomial evaluates at the
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: point to the measured value, and otherwise equals the overlap of the line
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: projector alone. This is the interchanged form of
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: `stateQForm_eprState_tauLineProj_tauPointProj`, supporting
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: `def:expanded-line-measurement`, paper
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:527-532`. -/
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: /-! ## Perfect consistency on an EPR pair -/
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: /-- Acting with the same Pauli line projector on both halves of the EPR state
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: equals acting on one half. Symmetry transports the right action to the left,
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: where idempotence absorbs the repeated projector. This is the perfect
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: ancillary consistency used in item 1 of `lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:527-532`. -/
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: /-- The EPR quadratic forms of the Pauli line projectors on one half sum to
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: one. Formalization-only auxiliary for the ancillary overlaps in
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: `lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:527-545`. -/
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: /-- The diagonal overlap of the two Pauli line measurements on an EPR pair is
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: one. Thus the ancillary measurement contributes no consistency defect. This
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: is the perfect ancillary consistency in item 1 of `lem:qld-comm-line-cons`,
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean: paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:527-532`. -/
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean: /-!
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean: # Self-consistency of the expanded line measurements
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean: 
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean: This module proves item 1 of the expanded-line consistency lemma on the two
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean: opposite-placement bipartitions. The strategy line measurements are
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean: self-consistent between the two players on average over the line-point
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean: distribution, because a disagreement on a sampled line is rejected by the
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean: corresponding self-loop of the Pauli basis test; the Pauli line projectors are
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean: perfectly consistent on an EPR pair; and the data-processing inequality
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean: transfers the product estimate to the addition postprocessing that defines the
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean: expanded line measurement.
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean: 
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean: The module also records that the error parameter of a projective setting is
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean: nonnegative, which is not assumed by the structure and is needed by the other
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean: two items as well.
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean: 
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean: ## References
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:

b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean: `lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, whose paper source is
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean: `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:527-532`.
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean: -/
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean: /-! ## Self-consistency of the unexpanded line measurements -/
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean: /-- Mismatch mass of the two folded line answers at one sampled line.
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean: Formalization-only auxiliary for the strategy input to item 1 of
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean: `lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean: `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:527-532`. -/

b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean: `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:527-532`. -/

b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean: item 1 of `lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
b/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean: `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:527-532`. -/

/-!
# Error inflation of restricted line-point averages

This module records how a nonnegative average over the line-point distribution
transfers to one restricted component.  The line-point law places weight
`1 / 2` on each of its two kinds and, inside each kind, weight `1 / m` on each
coordinate index, so every restricted component carries mixture weight
`1 / (2 m)` and a nonnegative average inflates by at most `2 m`.

## References

The estimates are items 1 and 2 of blueprint
`lem:restricted-line-mixture-bounds`, formalizing the unlabelled estimates at
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1052-1058`.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

open MIPStarRE.LDT hiding Measurement

noncomputable section

/-! ## Averages of the distribution operations -/

/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: an average against a dependent bind is the
iterated average.  Blueprint `lem:restricted-line-mixture-bounds`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1052-1058`. -/
theorem avgOver_bind {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
    (μ : Distribution α) (ν : α → Distribution β) (f : β → ℝ) :
    avgOver (Distribution.bind μ ν) f =
      avgOver μ (fun a => avgOver (ν a) f) := by
  classical
  unfold avgOver
  have h1 : ∀ b : β, (∑ a ∈ μ.support, μ.weight a * (ν a).weight b) * f b =
      ∑ a ∈ μ.support, μ.weight a * ((ν a).weight b * f b) := by
    intro b
    rw [Finset.sum_mul]
    exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => by ring
  change (∑ b ∈ μ.support.biUnion (fun a => (ν a).support),
    (∑ a ∈ μ.support, μ.weight a * (ν a).weight b) * f b) = _
  rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b _ => h1 b, Finset.sum_comm]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a ha => ?_
  rw [← Finset.mul_sum]
  congr 1
  refine (Finset.sum_subset ?_ ?_).symm
  · intro b hb
    exact Finset.mem_biUnion.mpr ⟨a, ha, hb⟩
  · intro b _ hb
    rw [(ν a).outsideSupport b hb, zero_mul]

/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: an average against a convex mixture is the
convex combination of the two averages.  Blueprint
`lem:restricted-line-mixture-bounds`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1052-1058`. -/
theorem avgOver_mix {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α] (t : ℝ) (ht0 : 0 ≤ t)
    (ht1 : t ≤ 1) (μ ν : Distribution α) (f : α → ℝ) :
    avgOver (Distribution.mix t ht0 ht1 μ ν) f =
      t * avgOver μ f + (1 - t) * avgOver ν f := by
  classical
  unfold avgOver
  have hsplit : (∑ a ∈ μ.support ∪ ν.support,
        (t * μ.weight a + (1 - t) * ν.weight a) * f a) =
      t * (∑ a ∈ μ.support ∪ ν.support, μ.weight a * f a) +
        (1 - t) * (∑ a ∈ μ.support ∪ ν.support, ν.weight a * f a) := by
    rw [Finset.mul_sum, Finset.mul_sum, ← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
    exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => by ring
  have hμ : (∑ a ∈ μ.support ∪ ν.support, μ.weight a * f a) =
      ∑ a ∈ μ.support, μ.weight a * f a := by
    refine (Finset.sum_subset Finset.subset_union_left ?_).symm
    intro a _ ha
    rw [μ.outsideSupport a ha, zero_mul]
  have hν : (∑ a ∈ μ.support ∪ ν.support, ν.weight a * f a) =
      ∑ a ∈ ν.support, ν.weight a * f a := by
    refine (Finset.sum_subset Finset.subset_union_right ?_).symm
    intro a _ ha
    rw [ν.outsideSupport a ha, zero_mul]
  change (∑ a ∈ μ.support ∪ ν.support,
    (t * μ.weight a + (1 - t) * ν.weight a) * f a) = _
  rw [hsplit, hμ, hν]

/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: an average against a product law is the
iterated average.  Blueprint `lem:restricted-line-mixture-bounds`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1056-1058`. -/
theorem avgOver_prod {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    (μ : Distribution α) (ν : Distribution β) (f : α × β → ℝ) :
    avgOver (Distribution.prod μ ν) f =
      avgOver μ (fun a => avgOver ν (fun b => f (a, b))) := by
  classical
  unfold avgOver
  change (∑ p ∈ μ.support ×ˢ ν.support, μ.weight p.1 * ν.weight p.2 * f p) = _
  rw [Finset.sum_product]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
  rw [Finset.mul_sum]
  exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b _ => by ring

/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: one component of a uniform mixture carries at
most the whole nonnegative average, scaled by its mixture weight.  Blueprint
`lem:restricted-line-mixture-bounds`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1052-1056`. -/
theorem avgOver_bind_uniform_component_le {ι β : Type*}
    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Nonempty ι] [DecidableEq β]
    (ν : ι → Distribution β) (f : β → ℝ) (hf : ∀ b, 0 ≤ f b) (i : ι) :
    1 / (Fintype.card ι : ℝ) * avgOver (ν i) f ≤
      avgOver (Distribution.bind (uniformDistribution ι) ν) f := by
  classical
  rw [avgOver_bind]
  have hterm : ∀ j ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset ι),
      0 ≤ (uniformDistribution ι).weight j * avgOver (ν j) f := fun j _ =>
    mul_nonneg ((uniformDistribution ι).nonnegative j) (avgOver_nonneg _ _ hf)
  have hsingle := Finset.single_le_sum
    (f := fun j => (uniformDistribution ι).weight j * avgOver (ν j) f)
    hterm (Finset.mem_univ i)
  rw [uniformDistribution_weight_apply] at hsingle
  exact hsingle

/-! ## Inflation of a restricted line-point average -/

/-- Restricting a nonnegative line-point average to one kind and one coordinate
index inflates it by at most `2 m`.  This is the pointwise form of item 1 of
blueprint `lem:restricted-line-mixture-bounds`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1052-1056`. -/
theorem avgOver_restrictedLinePointDist_le {P : AdmissibleParams}
    (f : (LineDesc P.toLdParams × (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)) → ℝ)
    (hf : ∀ sample, 0 ≤ f sample) (kind : LineKind) (i : Fin P.m) :
    avgOver (restrictedLinePointDist P kind i) f ≤
      2 * (P.m : ℝ) * avgOver (linePointDist P.toLdParams) f := by
  classical
  haveI : Nonempty (Fin P.m) :=
    Fin.pos_iff_nonempty.mp (lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one P.one_le_m)
  have hm : (0 : ℝ) < (P.m : ℝ) := by
    exact_mod_cast lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one P.one_le_m
  have hAnonneg : 0 ≤ avgOver (aLinePointDist P.toLdParams) f :=
    avgOver_nonneg _ _ hf
  have hDnonneg : 0 ≤ avgOver (dLinePointDist P.toLdParams) f :=
    avgOver_nonneg _ _ hf
  have hmixture : avgOver (linePointDist P.toLdParams) f =
      1 / 2 * avgOver (aLinePointDist P.toLdParams) f +
        (1 - 1 / 2) * avgOver (dLinePointDist P.toLdParams) f :=
    avgOver_mix _ _ _ _ _ f
  -- Each kind is bounded by twice the full line-point average.
  have hsum : 2 * avgOver (linePointDist P.toLdParams) f =
      avgOver (aLinePointDist P.toLdParams) f +
        avgOver (dLinePointDist P.toLdParams) f := by
    rw [hmixture]
    ring
  have hAle : avgOver (aLinePointDist P.toLdParams) f ≤
      2 * avgOver (linePointDist P.toLdParams) f := by
    rw [hsum]
    exact le_add_of_nonneg_right hDnonneg
  have hDle : avgOver (dLinePointDist P.toLdParams) f ≤
      2 * avgOver (linePointDist P.toLdParams) f := by
    rw [hsum]
    exact le_add_of_nonneg_left hAnonneg
  -- The coordinate index contributes a further factor `m`.
  have hcomponent : ∀ (ν : Fin P.m → Distribution (LineDesc P.toLdParams ×
      (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P))) (μ : Distribution (LineDesc P.toLdParams ×
      (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P))),
      μ = Distribution.bind (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m)) ν →
      avgOver μ f ≤ 2 * avgOver (linePointDist P.toLdParams) f →
      avgOver (ν i) f ≤ 2 * (P.m : ℝ) * avgOver (linePointDist P.toLdParams) f := by
    intro ν μ hbind hle
    have hcomp := avgOver_bind_uniform_component_le ν f hf i
    rw [Fintype.card_fin, ← hbind] at hcomp
    have hstep : avgOver (ν i) f ≤ (P.m : ℝ) * avgOver μ f := by
      rw [div_mul_eq_mul_div, one_mul, div_le_iff₀ hm] at hcomp
      rw [mul_comm]
      exact hcomp
    calc avgOver (ν i) f ≤ (P.m : ℝ) * avgOver μ f := hstep
      _ ≤ (P.m : ℝ) * (2 * avgOver (linePointDist P.toLdParams) f) := by
          exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hle (le_of_lt hm)
      _ = 2 * (P.m : ℝ) * avgOver (linePointDist P.toLdParams) f := by ring
  cases kind with
  | axis =>
      exact hcomponent (restrictedALineDist P.toLdParams) _
        (aLinePointDist_eq_bind_restricted P.toLdParams) hAle
  | diagonal =>
      exact hcomponent (restrictedDLineDist P.toLdParams) _
        (dLinePointDist_eq_bind_restricted P.toLdParams) hDle

/-- Restricting a nonnegative average over two independent line-point samples
to one kind and coordinate index in each factor inflates it by at most
`4 m ^ 2`.  This is the pointwise form of item 2 of
blueprint `lem:restricted-line-mixture-bounds`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1056-1058`. -/
theorem avgOver_prod_restrictedLinePointDist_le {P : AdmissibleParams}
    (f : ((LineDesc P.toLdParams × (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)) ×
      (LineDesc P.toLdParams × (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P))) → ℝ)
    (hf : ∀ sample, 0 ≤ f sample) (kindX kindZ : LineKind) (i j : Fin P.m) :
    avgOver (Distribution.prod (restrictedLinePointDist P kindX i)
        (restrictedLinePointDist P kindZ j)) f ≤
      4 * (P.m : ℝ) ^ 2 * avgOver (Distribution.prod
        (linePointDist P.toLdParams) (linePointDist P.toLdParams)) f := by
  classical
  have hfactor : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 2 * (P.m : ℝ) := by positivity
  rw [avgOver_prod, avgOver_prod]
  have hinner : ∀ s1 : LineDesc P.toLdParams × (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P),
      avgOver (restrictedLinePointDist P kindZ j) (fun s2 => f (s1, s2)) ≤
        2 * (P.m : ℝ) *
          avgOver (linePointDist P.toLdParams) (fun s2 => f (s1, s2)) :=
    fun s1 => avgOver_restrictedLinePointDist_le
      (fun s2 => f (s1, s2)) (fun s2 => hf (s1, s2)) kindZ j
  calc avgOver (restrictedLinePointDist P kindX i)
        (fun s1 => avgOver (restrictedLinePointDist P kindZ j)
          (fun s2 => f (s1, s2)))
      ≤ avgOver (restrictedLinePointDist P kindX i)
          (fun s1 => 2 * (P.m : ℝ) *
            avgOver (linePointDist P.toLdParams) (fun s2 => f (s1, s2))) :=
        avgOver_mono _ _ _ hinner

     4	# The sandwich POVM of the expanded point measurements
     5	
     6	The first step of the proof of `lem:qld-4-10` combines the two expanded point
     7	measurements into the sandwich POVM
     8	`R^{x,z}_{a,b} = M^{(Point,Z),z}_b M^{(Point,X),x}_a M^{(Point,Z),z}_b`.  The
     9	source forms it from the binary refinements; here it is formed directly with
    10	outcomes in `F_q × F_q`, which the Parseval transfer of
    11	`MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/Commutation.lean` makes possible.  This file
    12	defines the POVM, proves that it is close to the ordered product
    13	`M^Z_b M^X_a` by the approximate commutation, and records the consistency of
    14	the ordered products across opposite register placements, which follows from
    15	the self-consistency of each factor.
    16	
    17	## Main results
    18	
    19	* `ProjectiveSetting.sandwichPoint`: the sandwich POVM.
    20	* `sandwichPoint_ordered_dist_le`: closeness of the sandwich to the ordered
    21	  product on every placement, with the error of `lem:qld-comm-cons`.
    22	* `ordered_cross_dist_le`: the ordered product on one placement is close to
    23	  the reversed ordered product on the opposite placement.
    24

    28	(the sandwich and display `eq:qld-r-2`), blueprint
    29	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:803-960` (`lem:qld-4-10`); the
    30	route is explained in `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_combined-points-direct.tex`.

    46	/-- An expanded point effect is self-adjoint. -/
    47	theorem pointMeasExp_effect_conjTranspose (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
    48	    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
    49	    (a : PauliScalar P) :
    50	    ((S.pointMeasExp side W u).effect a)ᴴ = (S.pointMeasExp side W u).effect a :=
    51	  (S.pointMeasExp_isProjective side W u a).isSelfAdjoint.isHermitian.eq
    52	
    53	/-- An expanded point effect is idempotent. -/
    54	theorem pointMeasExp_effect_mul_self (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
    55	    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
    56	    (a : PauliScalar P) :
    57	    (S.pointMeasExp side W u).effect a * (S.pointMeasExp side W u).effect a =
    58	      (S.pointMeasExp side W u).effect a :=
    59	  (S.pointMeasExp_isProjective side W u a).isIdempotentElem.eq

    61	/-- The sandwich `M^Z_b M^X_a M^Z_b` is `(M^X_a M^Z_b)ᴴ (M^X_a M^Z_b)`. -/
    62	theorem sandwich_eq_conjTranspose_mul_self (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
    63	    (side : PlayerSide) (x z : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (a b : PauliScalar P) :
    64	    (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b * (S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect a *
    65	        (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b =
    66	      ((S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect a * (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b)ᴴ *
    67	        ((S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect a * (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b) := by
    68	  rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, pointMeasExp_effect_conjTranspose,
    69	    pointMeasExp_effect_conjTranspose, Matrix.mul_assoc _ _
    70	      ((S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect a * (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b),
    71	    ← Matrix.mul_assoc ((S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect a)
    72	      ((S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect a), pointMeasExp_effect_mul_self,
    73	    ← Matrix.mul_assoc]

    75	/-- The sandwich effects resolve the identity. -/
    76	theorem sum_sandwich_eq_one (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
    77	    (x z : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
    78	    ∑ ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P,
    79	        (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect ab.2 *
    80	          (S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect ab.1 *
    81	          (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect ab.2 = 1 := by
    82	  rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type_right]
    83	  calc ∑ b : PauliScalar P, ∑ a : PauliScalar P,
    84	        (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b * (S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect a *
    85	          (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b
    86	      = ∑ b : PauliScalar P, (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b *
    87	          (∑ a : PauliScalar P, (S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect a) *
    88	          (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b := by
    89	        refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b _ => ?_
    90	        rw [Finset.mul_sum, Finset.sum_mul]
    91	    _ = 1 := by
    92	        simp_rw [(S.pointMeasExp side .X x).sum_eq_one, mul_one,

    94	        exact (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).sum_eq_one

noncomputable def lineMeasExp (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
    (W : PauliKind) (line : LineDesc P.toLdParams) :
    Measurement (DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d))
      (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side) :=
  Measurement.ofSumEqOne (S.expLineOp side W line)
    (S.expLineOp_nonneg side W line) (S.expLineOp_sum_eq_one side W line)

/-- The effects of the expanded line measurement are the convolution
operators. -/
@[simp] theorem lineMeasExp_effect (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (line : LineDesc P.toLdParams)
    (f : DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d)) :
    (S.lineMeasExp side W line).effect f = S.expLineOp side W line f := rfl

/-- The fine product measurement underlying the convolution definition of an
expanded line measurement. Its outcome records the strategy and Pauli line
polynomials separately. Paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:527-532`. -/
noncomputable def lineTauMeas (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
    (W : PauliKind) (line : LineDesc P.toLdParams) :
    Measurement (DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d) ×
      DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d)) (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side) :=
  Measurement.ofSumEqOne
    (fun p => heteroKron ((S.lineMeas side W line).effect p.1)
      ((tauLineMeas P W line).effect p.2))
    (fun p => Quantum.kronecker_nonneg
      ((S.lineMeas side W line).pos p.1) ((tauLineMeas P W line).pos p.2))
    (by
      change ∑ p : DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d) ×
          DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d),
          heteroKron ((S.lineMeas side W line).effect p.1)
            (tauLineProj P W line p.2) = 1

        (∑ x, ∑ y, heteroKron ((S.lineMeas side W line).effect x)
            (tauLineProj P W line y)) =
            heteroKron (∑ x, (S.lineMeas side W line).effect x)
              (∑ y, tauLineProj P W line y) := (heteroKron_sum_sum _ _).symm
        _ = 1 := by
          rw [(S.lineMeas side W line).sum_eq_one, sum_tauLineProj_eq_one]
          exact heteroKron_one_one)

/-- Effects of the fine product measurement are the corresponding Kronecker
products of strategy and Pauli line effects. -/
@[simp] theorem lineTauMeas_effect (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (line : LineDesc P.toLdParams)
    (p : DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d) × DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d)) :
    (S.lineTauMeas side W line).effect p =
      heteroKron ((S.lineMeas side W line).effect p.1)
        (tauLineProj P W line p.2) := rfl

/-- The expanded line measurement is the addition postprocessing of its fine
strategy--Pauli product measurement. This is the data-processing presentation
used in item 1 of `lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:527-532`. -/
theorem lineMeasExp_effect_eq_lineTauMeas_postprocess
    (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind)
    (line : LineDesc P.toLdParams) (f : DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d)) :
    (S.lineMeasExp side W line).effect f =
      ((S.lineTauMeas side W line).postprocess
        (fun p => p.1 + p.2)).effect f := by
  change S.expLineOp side W line f = _
  rw [MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect]
  rfl

/-- An expanded line effect is idempotent: the strategy line projectors and
the Pauli line projectors are both orthogonal families, so distinct
convolution terms annihilate one another. This is the projectivity
calculation of `def:expanded-line-measurement`, paper
`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:552-556`. -/
private theorem expLineOp_mul_self (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (line : LineDesc P.toLdParams)
    (f : DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d)) :
    S.expLineOp side W line f * S.expLineOp side W line f =
      S.expLineOp side W line f := by
  have hM := S.lineMeas_isProjective side W line
  unfold expLineOp
  set s := Finset.univ.filter
    (fun pair : DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d) ×
        DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d) => pair.1 + pair.2 = f) with hs
  let K : DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d) ×
      DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d) → Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side) :=
    fun p => heteroKron ((S.lineMeas side W line).effect p.1)
      (tauLineProj P W line p.2)
  change (∑ p ∈ s, K p) * (∑ q ∈ s, K q) = ∑ p ∈ s, K p
  calc
    (∑ p ∈ s, K p) * (∑ q ∈ s, K q) = ∑ p ∈ s, ∑ q ∈ s, K p * K q := by
      rw [Finset.sum_mul]
      simp_rw [Finset.mul_sum]
    _ = ∑ p ∈ s, ∑ q ∈ s, if q = p then K p else 0 := by
      refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun p _ => Finset.sum_congr rfl fun q _ => ?_
      simp only [K]
      rw [heteroKron_mul]
      by_cases hqp : q = p
      · subst hqp
        rw [if_pos rfl, (hM q.1).isIdempotentElem.eq,
          tauLineProj_mul_tauLineProj, if_pos rfl]
      · rw [if_neg hqp]
        by_cases h1 : p.1 = q.1
        · have h2 : p.2 ≠ q.2 := fun h2 => hqp (Prod.ext h1.symm h2.symm)
          rw [tauLineProj_mul_tauLineProj, if_neg h2, heteroKron_zero_right]
        · rw [DistanceCalculus.projective_effect_mul_effect_eq_zero _ hM h1,
            heteroKron_zero_left]
    _ = ∑ p ∈ s, K p := by
      refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun p hp => ?_
      simp [hp]

/-- The expanded line measurement is projective. This is the projectivity
assertion in `def:expanded-line-measurement`, paper
`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:552-556`. -/
theorem lineMeasExp_isProjective (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (line : LineDesc P.toLdParams) :
    MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (S.lineMeasExp side W line) := by
  intro f
  refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
  · change S.expLineOp side W line f * S.expLineOp side W line f =
      S.expLineOp side W line f
    exact expLineOp_mul_self S side W line f
  · change star (S.expLineOp side W line f) = S.expLineOp side W line f

6:This module records the elementary calculus of the partial evaluation
7:`evalOpt` of a coefficient-list line polynomial at a point: the evaluation of
8:a sum is the sum of the evaluations whenever both summands evaluate, a summand
9:of an evaluating sum evaluates whenever the other summand does, the value is
10:unique, and nothing evaluates at a point off the line. These facts underlie
11:the manipulation of the evaluation classes in items 2 and 3 of the
12:expanded-line consistency lemma.

15:these facts about evaluation without stating them.

21:manipulated in `eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons` and `eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons2`,
22:paper `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:534-545`.

\section{At a glance}

\textbf{Difficulty.} The domain correction is elementary; the remaining
formal estimate requires the project's state-dependent Cauchy--Schwarz and
restricted-distribution arguments. \textbf{Estimated weight.} The correction
affects two Lean modules and their blueprint correspondence. It retains the
unfinished scalar estimate and isolates the existing pasting consistency
obligation. \textbf{Mathlib/project split.} Finite sums, positivity, and real
square roots use Mathlib; the measurement construction and subline law use
the local quantum API. \textbf{Key mathematical inputs.} Completeness of a
POVM, projectivity, and Cauchy--Schwarz suffice for the counterexample and
the proposed source proof. The counterexample below is a mathematical
calculation, not a kernel-certified Lean instance.

\section{Key theorem forms}

Let $\widehat\psi$ be the normalized expanded state of a projective strategy
winning the Pauli basis test with probability at least $1-\eps$. Write
$L^W_f(\ell)$ and $M^W_a(u)$ for its expanded line and point effects. For
the subline law $D$, abbreviate the two correlations by
\begin{align*}
 A(T)&=\E_D\E_{(x,z,\alpha,\beta)\in\ell}
   \sum_{f_X,f_Z}\langle\widehat\psi,
   (T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}\ot
     M^Z_{f_Z(z)}(z)M^X_{f_X(x)}(x))\widehat\psi\rangle,\\
 B(T)&=\E_D\E_{(x,z,\alpha,\beta)\in\ell}
   \sum_{f_X,f_Z}\langle\widehat\psi,
   (T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}\ot
     M^Z_{f_Z(z)}(z))\widehat\psi\rangle.
\end{align*}
The paper's Claim 17-2 states
\[
 |A(T)-B(T)|\leq O\bigl(m\sqrt{\delta_{\mathrm{Line}}(\eps)}\bigr)
 \quad\text{for}\quad
 T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}
 =L^X_{f_X}(\ell_X)L^Z_{f_Z}(\ell_Z)L^X_{f_X}(\ell_X).
\]
The former Lean declaration quantified instead over every paired-line POVM
with the degree support and evaluated consistency conclusions of the
combined-lines lemma. Its scalar errors $\delta_P,\delta_Q$ were arbitrary,
independently of $\eps$. The right-hand side remained the same, with
$\delta_{\mathrm{Line}}(\eps)=\sqrt\eps$.

\section{The construction used by the source}

The paired-line measurement is defined by the displayed sandwich in the
proof of the combined-lines lemma. Claim 17-2 uses this definition to sum
over the Z polynomial:
\[
 \sum_{f_Z}T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}
 =L^X_{f_X}(\ell_X)
   \Bigl(\sum_{f_Z}L^Z_{f_Z}(\ell_Z)\Bigr)L^X_{f_X}(\ell_X)
 =L^X_{f_X}(\ell_X).
\]
The last equality uses completeness and projectivity. Cauchy--Schwarz
reduces the scalar difference to the square root of the resulting
X-line/point consistency deficit. The separate X marginal of the subline
law is sufficient; no joint conditional law for $(x,z)$ is needed.
Restriction to a line kind and coordinate costs a factor $2m$, so the
resulting square-root estimate is bounded by the paper's stated error
because $m\geq1$.\footnote{The construction is at lines 942--949 and the
claim and calculation at lines 1168--1201 of
\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex},
labels \path{lem:qld-xz-lines} and \path{claim:17-2} in
\cite{Ji2020MIPStar}. The repair is tracked by \ghissue{414}; the earlier
proof attempt is \ghissue{405}.}

\section{A counterexample to the enlarged domain}

Choose an admissible tuple with $q>1$ and a perfect projective strategy.
The honest strategy in the completeness lemma supplies one; for example,
$(q,m,d)=(8,1,1)$ is admissible. Its expanded state has norm one. For
$a\in\F_q$, let $c_a$ be the constant polynomial with value $a$. For both
players and every line pair, define a POVM by
\[
 T_{c_a,c_b}=q^{-2}I\quad(a,b\in\F_q),\qquad
 T_{f_X,f_Z}=0\quad\text{for every other pair}.
\]
There are $q^2$ nonzero effects, so they sum to $I$. Both axis-degree
requirements hold. At any incident point a constant polynomial has a
uniquely determined value, even on a zero-direction line. Thus the optional
evaluation in Lean returns the ordinary field value, never an undefined
outcome, for every nonzero effect in this example.

The evaluated POVM is uniform on the $q^2$ point pairs. Against any complete
joint point measurement $Q$, its agreement is $q^{-2}$ and its consistency
defect is $1-q^{-2}$. Therefore the line-witness requirements hold with
$\delta_P=1$ in every opposite placement. A point witness also exists within
the former public domain: take the projective measurement which always
answers $(0,0)$. It is exactly self-consistent and has both ordered-product
distances at most $4$. Indeed, the squared norms of either ordered product
family sum to one, by projectivity and completeness, and
\begin{align*}
 \sum_{a,b}\|(Q_{a,b}-M^X_aM^Z_b)\widehat\psi\|^2
 &\leq 2\sum_{a,b}\|Q_{a,b}\widehat\psi\|^2\\
 &\quad+2\sum_{a,b}\|M^X_aM^Z_b\widehat\psi\|^2\\
 &=4.
\end{align*}
The reversed ordering satisfies the same calculation. Hence $\delta_Q=4$
is allowed by every point-witness field. These constants are permitted by
the former scalar quantifiers; the argument does not require them to be
polynomially small functions of $\eps$.

For each supported subline sample, completeness gives
\[
 A(T)=q^{-2}\sum_{a,b}\langle\widehat\psi,
    (I\ot M^Z_bM^X_a)\widehat\psi\rangle=q^{-2},
 \qquad
 B(T)=q^{-2}\sum_{a,b}\langle\widehat\psi,
    (I\ot M^Z_b)\widehat\psi\rangle=q^{-1}.
\]
The first equality uses $\sum_bM^Z_b\sum_aM^X_a=I$, without a commutation
assumption. Probability averaging preserves these constants. The absolute
difference is therefore $(q-1)/q^2>0$, whereas the claimed bound is zero at
$\eps=0$. For $q=8$ the difference is $7/64$. The same perfect strategy is
admissible at arbitrarily small positive $\eps$, so excluding zero or
enlarging a universal constant cannot repair the claim. No polynomially
vanishing error depending on $\eps$ alone absorbs this difference.

\section{Conclusion}

The discrepancy lies in the formal quantification over arbitrary witnesses,
not in the paper's constructed-measurement assertion. The counterexample
forces a domain correction. Using the defined sandwich restores the measurement domain. The complex
scalar conclusion is restored for the directly indexed auxiliary obligation;
transport to the source distribution and the consistency construction remain
open. The source claims themselves retain their complex-modulus statements
without unsupported formalization marks.

theorem SubLineWitness.one_sub_avgOver_zPointOverlap_le_at
    (sublines : SubLineWitness P) (lines : CombinedLinesWitness S points δP)
    (first second : Placement) (hopposite : first.IsOpposite second) :
    1 - avgOver sublines.D (fun sample =>
      avgOver (uniformDistribution (DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd))
        (fun t => zPointOverlapAt lines first second (sample.2, projZ (directPointToPauli P
          (sample.1.base + t • sample.1.direction))))) ≤
      2 * Real.sqrt (4 * (P.m : ℝ) ^ 2 * δP) + 2 * Real.sqrt (4 * δQ) := by
  obtain ⟨components, hcomp, hmix⟩ :=
    SubLineWitness.exists_avgOver_Z_eq_mixture P sublines (zPointOverlapAt lines first second)

        (restrictedLinePointDist P c.1 c.2.2))
        (fun w => zPointOverlapAt lines first second ((w.1.1, w.2.1), w.2.2))) =

          (restrictedLinePointDist P c.1 c.2.2))
          (fun w => zPointOverlapAt lines first second ((w.1.1, w.2.1), w.2.2))) := by
    rw [avgOver_sub, avgOver_const_of_isProbability components hcomp]
  rw [← hsplit]
  calc
    _ ≤ avgOver components (fun _ =>
